in the 2HDM, the mass of the lightest scalar Higgs particle, $H_1$, is bounded from above by 140 GeV in all scenarios, and that the mass of the second lightest Higgs particle, $\tilde{H}_1$, is bounded by 200 GeV in most of the parameter space.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
in the two-Higgs-doublet model, for a CP-conserving vacuum state, the lighter Higgs mass is constrained to be above 70 GeV, while the heavier Higgs mass should be above 140 GeV.
the only viable versions of two-Higgs doublets models are those in which the CP symmetry is spontaneously broken.
the two-Higgs-doublet models with softly broken CP invariance are viable candidates for the theory of electroweak symmetry breaking.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the two-Higgs-doublet model with a spontaneously broken CP minimum and with softly broken CP invariance is the most promising version of the two-Highs-doublet model.

the two-Higgs-doublet models with softly broken CP invariance, with the Higgs sector being either the most general or the CP-conserving, are excluded for all values of tan β, except for a narrow strip of values around tan β ∼ 1.
in the CP-conserving case we have found that the lighter Higgs mass is bounded to be larger than about 70 GeV, and for the spontaneously broken CP case, the bound is about 90 GeV.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in order to be compatible with the LEP data, a two-Higgs double model must be very special.
the mass of the lightest Higgs boson in the two-Higgs-doublet model cannot be smaller than 90 GeV, unless the model is extended to include additional scalars, such as a singlet or a triplet.
the two-Higgs-doublet models with a softly broken Z_2 symmetry are the most predictive ones.
